decode.title: Decode benchmark
decode.modelHint: Select which model the benchmark targets.
decode.noModels: No models are currently served by this target.
decode.thinkingHint: On by default. Reasoning tokens count toward decode tok/s.
decode.concurrencyHint: Levels run sequentially; each opens that many parallel streams.
decode.emptyBody: Pick a prompt type and concurrency levels, then run. Each level opens that many parallel streams and reports aggregate and per-stream decode tok/s.
decode.errorModel: Select a currently served model before running the benchmark
decode.errorConcurrency: Select at least one concurrency level
decode.errorMaxTokens: Max tokens must be an integer between 64 and 2048
decode.errorTemperature: Temperature must be a number between 0 and 2
decode.temperatureHint: Default 0.7 · 0 is greedy · 0 to 2. Before v2.70 the bench always ran at temp 0 with thinking off: set 0 to compare with those runs. Temp above 0 can be much slower on servers that use speculative decoding.
decode.contextHint: Each stream is prefilled to this many tokens first, then decodes from there. Needs prefix caching and KV room for concurrency × context.
decode.legend: Aggregate — total decode tok/s across all concurrent streams. Stream — per-stream average decode.
decode.mixedHistory: These runs use different temperature or thinking settings. Compare tok/s only between runs with the same settings; temp above 0 can be several times slower.

prefill.title: Prefill benchmark
prefill.contextHint: Type a custom token count to add it.
prefill.contextLimit: Model context {{context}} — larger sizes are disabled.
prefill.contextUnknownHint: Unique-prefix prompts; TTFT is time to first token. 128k–300k can take tens of minutes.
prefill.contextTooLarge: Does not fit the model context ({{context}} tokens) once the template and reply are added
prefill.errorCustomSize: Custom size must be an integer between {{min}} and {{max}} tokens (e.g. 131072 or 128k)
prefill.errorDoesNotFit: Custom size plus template and reply does not fit the model context ({{context}} tokens)
prefill.errorSelectFittingSize: Select at least one context size that fits this model
prefill.legend: Prefill — the server's own prompt-processing timing when it reports one, otherwise tokens computed ÷ (TTFT − calibrated request overhead), with prefix-cache hits excluded and the correction capped at half the TTFT. TTFT — request start to first streamed token. Tokens, TTFT and tok/s are from the median-rate sample of each size. Each size uses a unique prefix so prefix-cache does not inflate later sizes. Low confidence — the overhead was over 30% of the TTFT, so the rate leans on the calibration; n/m samples — some repeats failed.
prefill.emptyBody: Choose the context sizes to test, then run. Each size sends a unique prompt and reports prefill tok/s and time to first token.

quality.title: Quality benchmark
quality.concurrencyTitle: How many questions are sent to the model at the same time
quality.noSharedItems: No shared items between these runs.
quality.label: Label
quality.sameItems: Both runs passed and failed the same items.
quality.suiteHint: Fixed, seeded suite at temperature 0 — the same items every run, so runs pair item by item.
quality.example: Example (the shape of the real prompts)
quality.skippedLong: Skipped long sizes above the model context: {{sizes}}
quality.legend: Score — items passed. p — exact McNemar test on items only one run got right; p ≥ 0.05 means the difference is within noise. Items with a request error or timeout, replies cut off by max_tokens before an answer, and items with a disputed reference answer are not scored and are left out of the comparison. * — budget-limited: some replies were cut off, so the score covers only the ones that finished.
quality.budgetLimitedTitle: Some replies hit max_tokens before answering — this score covers only the replies that finished, so it is not a clean measurement under this budget
quality.truncatedTitle: Cut off by max_tokens before an answer — not scored
quality.disputedTitle: Disputed reference answer — reported, not scored
quality.emptyBody: Pick the categories to score, give the run a label (for example the quantisation or KV-cache format) and run. The suite is fixed and seeded, so any two runs can be compared item by item.
quality.deleteTitle: Delete this run from the history, keeping the other runs
quality.noiseFloorTitle: Run every category again at the same settings, and twice more at concurrency 1 when the run is batched, so run-to-run and batch noise are measured beside the score (2–4× the requests)
quality.noiseHint: Extra passes paired with the primary pass item by item. Flipped — the verdict changed; identical — the reply was byte-identical.
quality.coverageTitle: Scored ÷ total — the share of the category the score rests on. Budgeted — passed ÷ everything that ran, where a cut-off reply counts as not passed
quality.fidelityCompareHint: ΔNLL = this run − other run per token, positive means this run is worse; 95% interval over documents. Tail loss — how often the other run's most likely token is outside this run's top-K. The divergence is over the shared top-K with an "other" bucket: a coarse diagnostic, not a KL.
quality.fidelityMismatch: {{count}} document(s) tokenised differently and were not paired
quality.divNoCompare: The compared run has no divergence replies to pair with.
quality.divCompareHint: Reply identity measures how sensitive the output is to the serving stack, not whether it is correct: compare runs on the same engine and settings to read the differences as the build's. Edit distance is normalised over the first 1,200 characters; drift is read at character offsets of about 256, 1,024 and 2,048 tokens.
quality.compareGone: The run picked for comparison is no longer saved — it was deleted from the history, so if it was the pinned reference, pin another run
quality.pinTitle: The reference run of this model family: comparisons of any build of the model default to it, on every unit
quality.servingMismatch: The runs differ in {{keys}}: this compares serving configurations, not only weights.
quality.servingSame: Same unit, engine, build and settings on both sides: the differences are the weights'.
quality.quantSub: A = this run, B = the compared run
quality.quantHint: ΔNLL and perplexity from the fidelity corpus; identical replies, first divergence and loops from the divergence set; reasoning tokens and truncations over the generation categories both runs scored; per-category paired deltas with 95% intervals; decode tok/s from the last decode benchmark on the port (or the live probe) and memory from the probe at run start.
quality.quantPresetTitle: Arithmetic chain, state tracking, long-context recall, fidelity and divergence at concurrency 1: the categories that see a quantisation, without batching noise
quality.partialRunHint: Only the default and full profiles carry an overall score; this run scored {{categories}}.
quality.thinkingWarning: Thinking off was not honoured by {{model}} in {{category}}: {{reasoningRows}} of {{rows}} replies carried reasoning and {{truncated}} were cut off. This category's score reflects the budget, not the model.
quality.legendV2: Score — items passed, with a Wilson 95% interval; the overall carries a stratified bootstrap interval. Coverage — scored ÷ total; budgeted — passed ÷ everything that ran, so a model that truncates more cannot look better. p — exact McNemar test on the items only one run got right, Holm-adjusted across categories; p ≥ 0.05 is insufficient evidence of a difference, not equivalence. Equivalent — the paired delta's interval sits inside ±2 pts. A delta inside the run's measured noise floor reads as noise whatever p says. Items with a request error or timeout, replies cut off by max_tokens before an answer, and items with a disputed reference answer are not scored and are left out of the comparison. * — budget-limited: some replies were cut off, so the score covers only the ones that finished.
quality.verdictHint: Plain-words reading of the numbers below. A = {{a}}, B = {{b}}. "Better" means a difference beyond noise; "about the same" means no clear difference or one inside the measured noise floor.
quality.resumeTitle: Carry on from the next item
quality.pauseTitle: Replies already in flight finish and count; nothing new is sent until you resume. The run keeps its place, its results and its unit slot, and the clock stops.
quality.resumeRunTitle: Carry on with this run from the rows it already scored: a run killed by a server restart, stopped by an error streak or cancelled keeps those rows and runs only the rest. Fidelity is rerun. The time it was down is not counted.

compare.title: Pick two runs
compare.swapTitle: Exchange the two runs: deltas are always A minus B
compare.hint: A is read against B: a positive delta means A did better. Runs from different units or engine builds compare serving configurations, not only weights; the header says which keys differ.
compare.noRuns: No finished quality runs on any unit yet.
compare.emptyBody: Pick a run under test and a reference. When A's model family has a pinned reference, B is filled in for you.
